catalog_quote: Chamoreau 2023 p.6: "Stems end in a vowel and generally receive the accent on this vowel, that is, the accent indicates the morphological right edge of the stem. Nevertheless, the accent may sometimes appear on the first syllable of the stem: compare the examples in (1a-3a) where the first syllable is accented with (1b-3b) where the accent falls on the second syllable. I indicate the accent only when it appears on the first syllable. (1) a. wéra-ni ‘go out’ b. wera-ni ‘cry’ (2) a. kára-ni ‘fly’ b. kara-ni ‘write’ (3) a. píri-ni ‘approach’ b. piri-ni ‘sing’"; fn.3: "In these examples, we may observe that the final vowel is elided when it is not stressed. The accent appears on the first or second syllable of the stem." p.4 (scope): "...the different varieties of Purepecha, which are inter-intelligible to varying degrees, show two superimposed levels of organization ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding quotation in the record is verbatim at the stated locators in copies we hold (Chamoreau 2023 HAL ms p.6 + fn.3, scope p.4; Chamoreau 2005 fn.11 ms p.3; Bellamy 2018 p.19). (2) The deciding source is a 2023 specialist handbook sketch stating the rule for Purepecha as a whole; the record's own note flagged that no source described accent separately for the western varieties. (3) I downloaded the one open western-area phonology, Agustín Diego 2016 (CIESAS MA thesis, San Luis Tsuren, NW Sierra, municipio Los Reyes): it confirms the lexical coding exactly (σ1/σ2 root-internal left-edge window, lexically determined, σ2 majority 520 vs 222 of 749 words, minimal pairs kárani/karáni, accent immobile under suffixation) and refines it with material our record lacks: secondary stress every second syllable rightward from the primary, never final (syllabic trochee); diphthongs

sources.citation: Agustín Diego, Angélica. 2016. Fonología y procesos morfo-fonológicos del p'urhépecha de San Luis Tsuren. Tesis de maestría en Lingüística Indoamericana, CIESAS, México. 160 pp. (CIESAS repository handle 1015/608)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: San Luis Tsuren (municipio Los Reyes, NW Sierra = western area): 'la ventana acentual del p'urhépecha está restringida a la primera o segunda sílaba de la raíz, ubicada siempre a principio de palabra por la ausencia de morfología prefijal' (p.55); accent stays put under any suffixation (piréni, pirékuecha, ... p.60); 'sin ningún elemento visible que determine la elección sobre dónde colocar el acento mas que la cuestión léxica' (p.63); minimal pairs ˈka.ɾa.ni 'volar' vs ka.ˈɾa.ni 'escribir', ˈa.ɾi.ni vs a.ˈɾi.ni (p.63); corpus of 749 words: 222 with σ1 accent, 520 with σ2, 7 monosyllables, 'Pr
sources.locator: Cap. III 'Fonología prosódica: acento', printed pp.53-75; esp. pp.54-55 (window + exx. 1-5), pp.63-64 (minimal pairs, ex.13, Figs.3-4), pp.65-66 (corpus counts), pp.67-68 (secondary stress), p.72 (diphthongs), Tabla 8 p.74 (acoustics), conclusions p.75
sources.note: Only phonology of a western-area (Sierra) variety with a dedicated accent chapter (corpus counts 222 σ1 / 520 σ2, minimal pairs, secondary-stress rhythm, acoustics); our record rests on a pan-Purepecha handbook sketch and says secondary stress 'not described'.
